q: Kilometres run by an engine which is hauled as 'dead' in a train, that is, an engine in tow which is not itself working the train, are shown in operating statistics:

options.A: As train kilometres of the train in which the engine is hauled
options.B: Separately as dead engine kilometres, and not as train engine kilometres
options.C: As coaching vehicle kilometres of the train concerned
options.D: They are excluded from the engine kilometre statistics altogether

q: 'Seat kilometres' offered by the coaching services of a railway during a period represent:

options.A: The passenger kilometres actually performed by passengers during the period
options.B: The kilometres run by empty coaching stock between the depot and the station
options.C: The seating and berth capacity offered, worked out from the capacity of the coaches run and the distance run by them
options.D: The kilometres run by trains which carried no passengers during the period

q: The wagon stock of a railway is expressed in terms of four-wheeler units in the statistics mainly in order to:

options.A: Decide the class rate to be charged on goods carried in each wagon
options.B: Work out the tare weight of each individual wagon for charging freight
options.C: Fix the free time admissible for unloading wagons of different types
options.D: Bring wagons of different types and capacities, such as bogie wagons and four-wheeler wagons, to a common unit for comparison and accountal of wagon stock

q: 'Current reservation' at a station refers to the booking of accommodation which remains vacant in a train:

options.A: After the reservation chart of the train has been prepared, at the current booking counter or through the train staff, up to the departure of the train and thereafter as permitted
options.B: Exactly one year in advance of the date of journey
options.C: Only against the emergency quota released by the controlling officer
options.D: Only for season ticket holders travelling on the day of issue of the ticket

q: A 'remote location quota' in the Passenger Reservation System is a quota of reserved accommodation allotted to:

options.A: The train crew for their duty travel over the section
options.B: A station or location, other than the train's originating or chart-preparing location, from where reservations against that quota are controlled and issued
options.C: Passengers who book their tickets through the internet alone
options.D: The destination station of the train for allotment only after the train arrives

q: An 'Indrail Pass' on Indian Railways is a travel-as-you-like pass facility provided mainly for:

options.A: Season ticket holders of the suburban sections
options.B: Students travelling on educational tours within India
options.C: Foreign tourists, and non-resident Indians on their visit to India, entitling the holder to travel over Indian Railways for a specified period in the classes covered by the pass
options.D: Railway employees proceeding on duty from one station to another

q: Where a passenger reports, before the departure of the train, that his reserved ticket has been lost, a duplicate ticket may be issued to him:

options.A: Free of all charges in every case, on his oral statement alone
options.B: Only after the train has completed its journey and returned to the originating station
options.C: Only by the Railway Claims Tribunal on an application made to it
options.D: On his written application and on payment of the prescribed charges, subject to the conditions laid down for the issue of duplicate tickets in lieu of lost tickets

q: In the charging of passenger fares, a child below five years of age travelling with a passenger is, under the rules:

options.A: Carried free of charge, provided a separate seat or berth is not occupied for the child
options.B: Charged the full adult fare in every class of travel
options.C: Charged the fare of a season ticket for the section travelled
options.D: Permitted to travel only in the unreserved compartments of the train

q: Luggage found in a train or at a station which has been carried without being booked is dealt with at the destination by:

options.A: Confiscating it to the Railways without any charge on the owner
options.B: Charging it at the prescribed penal or enhanced scale over the ordinary luggage charges before it is delivered to the owner
options.C: Returning it free of charge to the station from which it was despatched
options.D: Delivering it without any charge, since the Railways cannot detect unbooked luggage

q: A pet dog accompanying a passenger is carried, under the rules, in the manner that:

options.A: It may be kept free of charge in any class of compartment chosen by the passenger
options.B: It is carried only as goods traffic on a Railway Receipt issued in the dog's name
options.C: It is carried in the dog box provided in the brake van, or, where the passenger travels in Air-conditioned First Class, it may accompany him in the compartment, in either case on payment of the prescribed charges
options.D: It is never accepted for carriage by a passenger train in any circumstances

q: For the carriage of a dead body by rail, the prescribed conditions require, broadly, that:

options.A: The body is carried as an ordinary parcel on a Parcel Way Bill without any accompanying document
options.B: The body is carried only in the luggage van of a goods train, unaccompanied by any person
options.C: No charge of any kind is levied, the carriage being treated as a free service
options.D: The body is properly enclosed and accompanied by the prescribed medical or death certificate and by an attendant, and is carried in a brake van or a carriage set apart for the purpose on payment of the prescribed charges

q: Luggage or articles deposited by the public in the cloak room of a station against a cloak room receipt are delivered back:

options.A: To the person who surrenders the cloak room receipt, after the charges due for the period of deposit have been paid
options.B: Only to the station master of the station at which the articles were booked
options.C: Only after a fresh luggage ticket is purchased for their onward journey
options.D: Free of all charges, at any time within one year of the deposit

q: The supply of bedrolls or linen to passengers in the air-conditioned classes of trains is arranged so that:

options.A: Passengers must always bring their own bedrolls, the Railways supplying none in any class
options.B: Bedrolls are supplied only in trains run by private operators and not in railway trains
options.C: Bedding is supplied to the passengers of the classes in which the facility is provided, its cost being covered in the fare structure or recovered as prescribed for the class and train concerned
options.D: Bedrolls are issued by the Travelling Inspector of Accounts during his station inspections

q: A Cash and Coin Operated Ticket Vending Machine installed at a station is used by passengers to:

options.A: Obtain refunds on cancelled reserved tickets in cash
options.B: Purchase unreserved tickets by themselves, on payment by cash, coin or the prescribed card, without going to the booking counter
options.C: Reserve accommodation in trains against the general quota
options.D: Pay the freight on goods consignments booked at the station

q: Hand Held Terminals issued to the ticket checking staff on trains enable them mainly to:

options.A: Print the Railway Receipts for goods booked at wayside stations
options.B: Compile the Accounts Office Balance Sheet while travelling on the train
options.C: Levy demurrage on wagons detained at the stations passed en route
options.D: Allot vacant berths and accommodation on the train to waiting passengers on board and feed the position back to the reservation system, instead of working only from the printed chart

q: Under the Parcel Management System, each parcel package booked is bar-coded at the station of booking mainly so that:

options.A: Its movement can be captured and traced at booking, loading, transhipment and delivery points through the system, instead of being followed only from paper records
options.B: The parcel can be exempted from payment of parcel charges at destination
options.C: The weight of the package need not be recorded on the Parcel Way Bill
options.D: The parcel can be carried only in trains fitted with parcel scanners

q: An electronic in-motion weighbridge installed on a railway serves mainly to:

options.A: Weigh only the locomotives of trains passing over it for maintenance statistics
options.B: Replace the Forwarding Note for consignments loaded in the yard
options.C: Weigh wagons of a moving rake without detaining or stopping the rake, the weighment data being used, among other things, for detecting overloading and passing the information to the freight information system
options.D: Work out the passenger kilometres performed by trains passing over it

q: 'Double-stack' container working on Indian Railways refers to the running of container trains in which:

options.A: Two container trains are coupled together and run as one train in every case
options.B: Two containers are carried one above the other on a flat wagon, so that a rake carries substantially more containers, the working requiring the prescribed clearances and overhead equipment height on the route
options.C: Containers are loaded in the upper berths of double-decker passenger coaches
options.D: Every container is weighed twice, once at booking and once at delivery

q: Station Ticket Booking Agents are engaged at small stations of the prescribed categories mainly to:

options.A: Conduct the internal check of the accounts of those stations
options.B: Sell platform tickets alone, and no other tickets, at those stations
options.C: Apportion the earnings of those stations among the zonal railways
options.D: Issue unreserved tickets at those stations on commission, so that ticketing facility is available at stations where the traffic does not justify a regular booking establishment

q: A Yatri Ticket Suvidha Kendra is a ticketing facility operated:

options.A: By licensed private agents at premises outside the station, authorised to issue reserved and unreserved tickets to the public on the prescribed charges and commission
options.B: By the Railway Claims Tribunal for parties to compensation cases
options.C: Only inside the parcel office of a station for booking parcels
options.D: Only on board trains by the ticket checking staff

q: 'Kisan Rail' trains on Indian Railways were introduced mainly to provide:

options.A: Free travel to farmers attending agricultural exhibitions in metropolitan cities
options.B: Parcel vans attached to passenger trains exclusively for the carriage of milk
options.C: Quick and dedicated movement of perishable agricultural produce, such as fruits and vegetables, from the producing areas to the consuming markets, with the concessions extended for such traffic as prescribed
options.D: Goods trains for the carriage of fertilisers alone at a uniform rate all over India

q: In the leasing of parcel space in trains, such as the luggage compartment of a train or a parcel van, the space is leased to a leaseholder who:

options.A: Becomes an employee of the Railways for the period of the lease
options.B: Books and carries parcels in the leased space during the lease period, on the lease terms obtained through tender or e-auction and on payment of the lease charges
options.C: Is exempted from all liability for the parcels carried in the leased space
options.D: Fixes the parcel rates for all stations of the railway during the lease period

q: Amounts realised by a railway from the sale of platform tickets at its stations are classified in the earnings accounts under:

options.A: Sundry other earnings of the railway
options.B: Goods earnings of the railway
options.C: Earnings from catering services of the railway
options.D: Coaching earnings of the railway

q: The benefit of trainload rates for a goods consignment is admissible only where:

options.A: The traffic is offered and carried in a full trainload or rake load satisfying the prescribed conditions for trainload movement, traffic not so offered being charged at the applicable wagonload or other rates
options.B: The consignor owns the wagons in which the traffic is loaded in every case
options.C: The destination station is situated on a different railway from the booking station
options.D: The freight on the consignment is left to be paid at the destination station

q: Goods which are light and bulky in proportion to their weight, and are prescribed to be charged on a measurement or volumetric basis, are charged freight:

options.A: Only on their tare weight as marked by the consignor
options.B: At a flat rate per package, irrespective of size and weight
options.C: On the chargeable weight derived from their dimensions in accordance with the prescribed volumetric conversion, where that basis is more favourable to revenue than the actual weight
options.D: Free of charge, since such goods occupy space but add little weight

q: An over-dimensional consignment offered for carriage by rail can be moved only where:

options.A: The consignor agrees in writing to pay double the normal freight in every case
options.B: Its movement is feasible on the route and is sanctioned beforehand by the competent authority, the consignment then being moved subject to the special conditions and restrictions imposed for its safe passage
options.C: It is loaded in the brake van of a passenger train to save time
options.D: The destination station certifies that it has a crane of sufficient capacity

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The average speed of goods trains, as worked out in the operating statistics, is derived from the train kilometres performed and the train hours taken.
2. Train hours for this purpose take into account the detentions suffered by the trains en route and at intermediate stations.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

q: 'Tonnes per wagon loaded', as an operating statistic, is worked out as:

options.A: The tonnes originating on the railway divided by the number of wagons loaded, giving the average load obtained per wagon loaded
options.B: The Net Tonne Kilometres performed divided by the train kilometres run
options.C: The Gross Tonne Kilometres performed divided by the wagon kilometres run
options.D: The tonnes carried divided by the number of engines in use on the railway

q: A 'rake link' in coaching operations is a document or arrangement which shows:

options.A: The list of passengers allotted berths in a rake on its first run
options.B: The charges recoverable for the use of a goods rake by a private siding
options.C: The programmed working of a coaching rake from trip to trip, linking its arrivals and departures, so that the rake is utilised in a planned cycle with its maintenance provided at the proper place
options.D: The apportionment of the earnings of a rake among the railways over which it runs

q: The 'primary maintenance' of a coaching rake is carried out:

options.A: At every station at which the train terminates, by the station staff on duty
options.B: At the rake's home or primary depot, where the rake is given its full maintenance examination and attention in accordance with its link, the examination at the other end of the run being of the prescribed secondary nature
options.C: Only in the workshop to which the rake is sent for periodical overhaul
options.D: By the train crew while the train is standing at the originating platform

q: A coach which is found to require repairs or attention before it can be run in a train is detached and placed in the sick line, from where it is:

options.A: Sold to the public by auction at the station itself
options.B: Returned to service immediately at the next departure of any train
options.C: Counted as a vehicle in use for all the days it spends in the sick line
options.D: Attended to and repaired, and offered for traffic again only after it is certified fit to run

q: Rolling stock on a railway is normally condemned and disposed of when:

options.A: It has completed its prescribed codal life, or its repair has become uneconomical, and its condemnation is sanctioned by the competent authority
options.B: It has remained idle in a yard for more than seven days at a stretch
options.C: The Travelling Inspector of Accounts recommends its condemnation in his inspection report
options.D: A new series of stock of the same type is inducted on the railway

q: The Control Office Application of Indian Railways supports train operations mainly by:

options.A: Apportioning the earnings of every train among the zonal railways daily
options.B: Preparing the Station Balance Sheets of all stations on the controlled section
options.C: Capturing the running and control data of trains, which feeds, among other things, the passenger information systems about the running position of trains
options.D: Fixing the fares and freight rates to be charged on the controlled section

q: The Integrated Coaching Management System of Indian Railways is used mainly for monitoring:

options.A: The stock verification of stores depots holding coaching material
options.B: Coaching stock, including rake composition, train composition and the maintenance and punctuality-related information of coaching services
options.C: The catering contracts awarded at stations of a division
options.D: The claims preferred for damage to coaching consignments

q: A consignment was entrusted to a railway for carriage and, more than six months later, the party prefers a claim for compensation for its non-delivery for the first time, without having preferred any claim in writing within that period. The correct position under Section 106 of the Railways Act, 1989 is that:

options.A: The claim must be entertained, since the Limitation Act alone governs such claims
options.B: The railway must pay the claim after obtaining the sanction of the Railway Claims Tribunal
options.C: The station master may entertain the claim if the amount involved is small
options.D: The party is not entitled to the compensation, the claim not having been preferred in writing to the railway administration within six months from the date on which the goods were entrusted for carriage

q: A station deposits its earnings with the bank on the last day of a month, but the amount is credited to the Railways' bank account only in the following month. In the accounts of the month of deposit, this amount is correctly shown as:

options.A: Cash-in-Transit, since the earnings have been remitted by the station but have not yet been credited to the Railways' account
options.B: A station outstanding recoverable from the Station Master personally
options.C: Sundry other earnings of the following month
options.D: A debit under Traffic Suspense to be written off at the year end

q: As between the internal check in the Traffic Accounts Office and an inspection by the Travelling Inspector of Accounts, the correct distinction is that:

options.A: Both are carried out only at the station premises
options.B: The internal check is exercised in the Accounts Office on the accounts rendered by the station, while the Travelling Inspector verifies matters on the spot at the station
options.C: The internal check is exercised by the Commercial Department, while the inspection is exercised by the Audit Department
options.D: Neither involves any examination of the earnings accounted for by the station

q: A hoarding contract is let at a station situated wholly on one zonal railway and the advertisement charges are recovered there. The correct treatment of these earnings in apportionment is that they are:

options.A: Apportioned among all zonal railways in proportion to route kilometres
options.B: Apportioned among the railways in proportion to the distance of traffic carried
options.C: Retained wholly by the railway on which they arise, sundry earnings not being subject to distance apportionment
options.D: Credited to the Railway Board and excluded from the zonal railway's earnings

q: During check of a goods invoice, the Traffic Accounts Office finds that a merchant was charged freight in excess of the amount due, though the merchant has filed no claim. The amount is dealt with by:

options.A: Crediting it to sundry earnings of the station
options.B: Adjusting it against the undercharges of other merchants
options.C: Retaining it till the merchant prefers a formal claim
options.D: Preparing an overcharge sheet so that the excess can be refunded to the party entitled

q: A station pays a handling contractor under proper authority and supports the debit taken in its Station Balance Sheet with the document known as a:

options.A: Paid voucher, evidencing the payment made on behalf of the Railways
options.B: Cash remittance note
options.C: Error sheet issued by the Traffic Accounts Office
options.D: Overcharge sheet prepared for the contractor

q: A consignee refuses to take delivery of a consignment on its arrival at destination and the consignor, though advised, gives no disposal instructions. The consignment is thereafter dealt with as:

options.A: Traffic to be returned free of charge to every station it passed
options.B: An unclaimed consignment, after due notice and in accordance with the prescribed procedure
options.C: The property of the destination station staff
options.D: A departmental consignment of the Railways

q: In the Passenger Reservation System, the waitlist category abbreviated as PQWL is the waitlist of the:

options.A: Premium Quota
options.B: Passenger Quota
options.C: Pooled Quota
options.D: Platform Quota

q: The Station Outstanding Register maintained in connection with station accounts serves mainly to:

options.A: Record the daily running position of trains at the station
options.B: Register the tickets printed for the station
options.C: Show the leave position of the station staff
options.D: Keep item-wise watch over the outstandings against the station until each item is cleared

q: Excess Fare Ticket books, Railway Receipt books and similar accountable forms supplied to a station are treated as money-value books, which means that:

options.A: Every book and foil must be accounted for, and missing foils are pursued as debits against the station
options.B: They may be replaced by locally printed forms whenever stock runs out
options.C: Their accountal is required only at the close of the financial year
options.D: Unused foils may be destroyed by the station without any record

q: On check of concession vouchers, the Traffic Accounts Office finds that a fare concession was allowed without the authority prescribed for it. The normal consequence in the station accounts is that:

options.A: The concession is regularised automatically by the passage of time
options.B: A debit is raised against the station for the amount of the concession irregularly allowed
options.C: The amount is charged to the passenger's next journey
options.D: The voucher is returned to the passenger for correction

q: Demurrage on a consignment was collected at destination and, on a later representation, the competent authority orders the amount to be returned to the party. In accounts terms, this transaction is a:

options.A: Waiver of demurrage, since the charge had not been paid
options.B: Fresh levy of wharfage on the same consignment
options.C: Refund of demurrage, since charges already collected are being repaid
options.D: Write-off of a station outstanding

q: A consignment reaches a destination station but its invoice and booking particulars have not been received, so it cannot be connected with any booking. Pending receipt of the particulars, the station should:

options.A: Auction the consignment on the day of its arrival
options.B: Deliver it to the first person who claims it
options.C: Return it to the forwarding station without recording it anywhere
options.D: Record it as an unconnected consignment and keep it under watch until it is connected with its booking

q: For passenger statistics, the journeys performed by season ticket holders are taken into account by:

options.A: Estimating the number of journeys on the prescribed standard basis, since each journey made on a season ticket is not separately recorded
options.B: Counting each season ticket sold as exactly one journey for the whole period of its validity
options.C: Omitting season ticket travel from the passenger statistics altogether
options.D: Counting only those journeys on which the ticket was checked on the train

q: A passenger buys one through ticket for a long journey instead of separate tickets for each part of it. Because passenger fares are charged on the telescopic principle, the through fare will ordinarily be:

options.A: Exactly equal to the sum of the fares for each separate part
options.B: Less than the sum of the fares for its parts, the rate per kilometre tapering with distance
options.C: Higher than the sum of the fares for its parts in every case
options.D: A flat amount independent of the distance of the journey

q: Before the earnings of a through goods consignment are divided among the carrying railways in proportion to distance, the share set apart for the railways which performed the loading and unloading services represents the:

options.A: Demurrage charges of the consignment
options.B: Sundry earnings of the terminal stations
options.C: Terminal charges for the services rendered at the terminals
options.D: Amount held under Traffic Suspense for the consignment

q: As between a Jansadharan Ticket Booking Sevak and a Station Ticket Booking Sevak, the correct distinction is that the Jansadharan sevak:

options.A: Works inside the booking office as a regular railway employee
options.B: Sells tickets only at the station to which he is posted on duty
options.C: Conducts the internal check of the station accounts
options.D: Sells unreserved tickets from his own premises outside the station, linked to the station to which he is attached

q: At the originating station, the cost of documenting a consignment, handling it and loading it into the wagon is, in traffic costing terms, a:

options.A: Terminal cost, being a cost incurred at the terminal in dealing with the traffic
options.B: Line haul cost, being the cost of hauling it between terminals
options.C: Capital cost of the terminal building
options.D: Cost to be charged wholly to coaching services

q: A statement shows the Net Tonne Kilometres performed on each route kilometre of a section. The index so shown is the:

options.A: Average lead of the traffic
options.B: Density of traffic on the section
options.C: Wagon turn-round of the section
options.D: Load factor of the trains on the section

q: A booking facility is provided at a place which is not served by a railway line, and traffic booked there is carried to and from the railhead station linked to it. Such a facility is an:

options.A: Assisted siding
options.B: City booking office within the station premises
options.C: Out agency
options.D: Private freight terminal

q: During a ticket-checking drive at a station, every exit is manned and the ticket of every passenger leaving the station is examined. Such an intensive check is known as a:

options.A: Census check
options.B: Surprise cash check
options.C: Stock verification
options.D: Fortress check

q: Rails and sleepers are despatched from one railway depot to a work site for the Railways' own use on a Railway Material Consignment note. The freight on this movement is:

options.A: Adjusted in the books by transfer, no cash freight being collected as commercial earnings
options.B: Collected in cash from the consignee and credited to goods earnings
options.C: Recovered from the contractor executing the work in every case
options.D: Written off as an irrecoverable station outstanding

q: A wagon owned by one zonal railway is loaded on another zonal railway for a destination on a third railway in the normal course. This is possible mainly because goods wagons of the zonal railways:

options.A: Are confined to the owning railway and are never interchanged
options.B: Form a common pool and are freely interchanged among the railways for loading
options.C: Are sold to the loading railway for each trip
options.D: Can be used by another railway only after condemnation by the owner

q:
Consider the following statements about the e-payment facility for freight:
1. It works under a tripartite arrangement among the Railways, the bank and the freight customer.
2. Under it, the freight is debited directly to the customer's bank account instead of being collected in cash at the goods shed.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: The cost of constructing a siding is shared between the Railways and the party for whom the siding is provided. Such a siding is classified as an:

options.A: Private siding, the whole cost being borne by the party
options.B: Departmental siding of the Engineering Department
options.C: Military siding maintained by the Defence authorities
options.D: Assisted siding

q: A Yatri Ticket Suvidha Kendra differs from a Jansadharan Ticket Booking Sevak mainly in that the Kendra is authorised to issue:

options.A: Reserved as well as unreserved tickets to the public from premises outside the station
options.B: Platform tickets alone
options.C: Railway Receipts for goods traffic alone
options.D: Season tickets alone

q: A consignment has arrived at destination but the freight and other charges due on it remain unpaid. The Railways may detain the consignment and exercise a lien on it until:

options.A: The close of the financial year in which it arrived
options.B: The freight and all other charges due in respect of the consignment are paid
options.C: The consignee files an appeal before the Claims Tribunal
options.D: The consignor executes a fresh Forwarding Note

q: Compensation paid by the Railways for the loss of a consignment is distinguished from a refund of overcharged freight in accounts mainly because compensation is:

options.A: Deducted from the goods earnings of the railway
options.B: Recovered from the destination station in every case
options.C: Charged to the working expenses of the Railways and is not deducted from earnings
options.D: Held under Traffic Suspense till the close of the year

q: As distinguished from gross earnings, gross receipts of a railway take into account, in addition to the earnings accrued:

options.A: Only the capital receipts of the railway
options.B: Only the earnings of the following year
options.C: The dividend payable to General Revenues
options.D: The suspense accounts connected with the traffic transactions

q: A material train carrying rails for a railway work runs on the line and performs Net Tonne Kilometres, but yields no traffic earnings. Such a train is classified in the statistics as a:

options.A: Departmental (non-revenue) train
options.B: Revenue-earning goods train
options.C: Coaching train
options.D: Mixed train for the public

q: Over a period, the diesel consumed by the goods locomotives of a railway falls while the Gross Tonne Kilometres performed by them remain the same. This fall in Specific Fuel Consumption indicates:

options.A: A deterioration in the fuel efficiency of the locomotives
options.B: An improvement in fuel efficiency, less fuel being consumed per 1000 Gross Tonne Kilometres
options.C: An increase in the number of locomotives under repair
options.D: A fall in the average load of goods trains

q: Net Tonne Kilometres per wagon day is an example of a derived statistic, because it is:

options.A: Collected directly from the forwarding notes of stations
options.B: A basic unit counted at the station, like the number of wagons loaded
options.C: Worked out as a ratio from the fundamental units of Net Tonne Kilometres and wagon days
options.D: Furnished by the passengers and merchants themselves

q: As between internal check and statutory audit of station accounts, the correct position is that statutory audit is exercised by:

options.A: The Traffic Accounts Office itself, as part of its internal check
options.B: The Commercial Department of the zonal railway
options.C: The Travelling Inspector of Accounts during his inspections
options.D: The Railway Audit organisation working under the Comptroller and Auditor General of India

q: A freight customer is allowed to load his rake at one point and unload it at two points, on the conditions prescribed for the facility. The facility availed of by him is the:

options.A: Two-point rake facility
options.B: Mini rake facility for short leads
options.C: Engine-on-load facility at the terminal
options.D: Roll-on roll-off facility

q: At a Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminal, the rail connectivity for moving the traffic is provided by the Railways, while the terminal and its handling facilities are developed:

options.A: Wholly at the cost of the passengers using the terminal
options.B: With private investment by the terminal developer
options.C: Only by the State Government in every case
options.D: Without any investment, on open railway land alone

q: A consignee holds an electronic Railway Receipt for his consignment and does not attend the goods shed merely to surrender a paper receipt. For taking delivery, he can use the facility of:

options.A: Filing a Ticket Deposit Receipt online
options.B: Registering a fresh indent in the system
options.C: E-surrender of the electronic Railway Receipt through the system
options.D: Obtaining a transfer certificate from the forwarding station

q: Two zonal railways settle the hire charges for wagons of one used by the other. The settlement is worked out primarily from:

options.A: The earnings collected by the user railway during the year
options.B: The number of wagons built by the owner railway
options.C: The staff strength of the interchange stations
options.D: The interchange records of the wagons handed over and received between the railways

q: A debit raised against a station is later found to be wholly irrecoverable. Such a debit can be written off only:

options.A: Under the sanction of the competent authority, with the concurrence of the Finance/Accounts branch
options.B: By the Station Master in the balance sheet of the following month
options.C: By the Travelling Inspector of Accounts at his next inspection
options.D: By adjustment against the demurrage collected at the station

q: A station considers that a debit advised to it through the Advice of Internal Check is incorrect. The proper course for the station is to:

options.A: Omit the debit from its balance sheet without informing the Accounts Office
options.B: Make a representation to the Traffic Accounts Office, on acceptance of which the debit is withdrawn or adjusted
